topic: Minimal edge-support obstruction hypergraphs for exact reliability of uncertain causal identification. Given a topologically ordered ADMG envelope with deterministic backbone edges, independently uncertain directed/bidirected edges, and a fixed query P_x(y), define O_XY as all inclusion-minimal uncertain-edge supports on which ordinary ID fails. Let b be the largest bidirected district of the full envelope and tau the incidence-treewidth of O_XY. Prove a canonical sparse-hedge-core algorithm enumerates O_XY with 2^{O(b log b)} polynomial preprocessing and delay, with coverage, global minimality, duplicate suppression, and exhaustion; include a complete polynomial-delay construction for all b<=2 envelopes by deterministic-path projection and induced-path branching. Prove R_XY(p)=product_e(1-p_e) I_O((p_e/(1-p_e))_e), compute R and every partial derivative in 2^{O(tau)} polynomial exact-arithmetic time from an incidence decomposition, and prove exact successful-realization counting at p_e=1/2 is #P-complete already at b=2. Consumer: Akbari et al.'s uncertain-ADMG sampler and edgeID workflow, which would report total identifiability probability, minimal failure combinations, and graph-refinement sensitivities instead of only one selected identifiable realization. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Informal derivations show that reachable-district width b equals the largest bidirected district of the envelope; every hedge has a selected core with at most 2b-2 edges and at most |V|*2^{O(b log b)} core templates. The entire b<=2 class reduces to labeled DAG reachability, where deterministic-path projection and chord-deleting induced-path branching enumerate minimal uncertain-edge supports with polynomial delay. Exact checks covered 32,000 four-vertex queries, 1,024 source-star realizations, 729 ternary DAG envelopes, 400 random seven-vertex envelopes, and 4,096 transversal encodings. The normalized independence-polynomial identity, incidence-treewidth reliability/derivative dynamic program, and #P hardness already at b=2 were also derived. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a canonical partial-support recursion for globally minimal multiple-root ancestry supports across competing sparse hedge cores with 2^{O(b log b)} preprocessing and worst-case delay, including deterministic projection, cross-core domination, duplicate suppression, and exhaustion. EARLY KILL TEST: Exhaustively compare the proposed root-ordered state and child partition against every minimal support on envelopes with at most six vertices, b<=3, and at most eight uncertain edges; any omission, duplicate, false live branch, or lost global minimality stops the compiler. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_minhedge_reliability_hypergraph.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can all inclusion-minimal uncertain-edge supports whose simultaneous presence makes a fixed ADMG query P_x(y) nonidentifiable be enumerated with delay fixed-parameter tractable in maximum district size, including polynomial delay throughout the b<=2 class?

source_refs.claim: The paper optimizes for a highest-plausibility identifiable graph under uncertain edges but does not enumerate minimal edge combinations causing ID failure.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Fateme Jamshidi, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Matthew J. Vowels, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Completeness of ordinary ID supplies hedge certificates for nonidentifiability in a fixed ADMG but no uncertain-edge support enumeration.
source_refs.author: Ilya Shpitser, Judea Pearl

source_refs.claim: Minimal hedges may be enumerated exponentially in the hedge-hull size, while the intervention-design algorithm uses lazy hedge discovery rather than output-sensitive edge-support enumeration.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Bounded-VC-dimension hypergraphs admit incremental-polynomial minimal-transversal enumeration, while general hypergraph dualization remains open.
source_refs.author: Arnaud Mary

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fixed-graph ID supplies a hedge witness, and intervention design manipulates vertex-minimal hedges inside one known graph, whereas uncertain realizations require edge-minimal supports across competing hedge cores. Supports generated from different cores can dominate one another, and distinct ancestry/path witnesses can generate the same support. Consequently, coverage, global rather than within-core minimality, duplicate suppression, exhaustion, and worst-case delay require a canonical cross-core recursion not present in the causal algorithms or in generic path, cut, and transversal enumeration.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A canonical sparse-hedge-core enumeration theorem with 2^{O(b log b)} polynomial preprocessing and delay, proofs of coverage, global minimality, uniqueness and exhaustion, and an explicit deterministic-path-projection and induced-path-branching algorithm for every b<=2 envelope.

writing_exemplar.why: Its uncertain-edge setup and edgeID workflow give the closest motivation and operational consumer for obstruction enumeration.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: causal identification assumes a correct ADMG -> practical graphs carry edge-level uncertainty -> edgeID selects one plausible identifiable realization -> enumerate every minimal edge combination that destroys identifiability

method_exemplars.technique: Refine the ID completeness argument that converts failed recursive district factorization into a hedge certificate so that it returns a sparse edge-labeled core.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired supports must be sound and complete for exactly the graph-native nonidentifiability predicate certified by hedges.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its canonical witness-extension and polynomial-delay branching for minimal directed path conjunctions to projected ancestry witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At district size two, the proposed hedge obstruction reduces to a labeled directed-reachability structure closely matching its path-conjunction machinery.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse hedge-hull reduction and lazy minimal-hedge discovery, replacing the optimization stopping rule with a globally minimal, duplicate-free support recursion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest causal algorithm that explicitly discovers minimal hedges and proves exactness of a combinatorial procedure over them.

open_problems.open_problem: Given the minimal nonidentifiability-support hypergraph of an uncertain ADMG query, can its exact identification probability and every edge-probability derivative be computed in time fixed-parameter tractable in support-edge incidence treewidth?

source_refs.claim: The probabilistic-ADMG framework optimizes selected identifiable graphs or formulas but does not sum the probability of all identifiable realizations or compute its gradient.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Fateme Jamshidi, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Matthew J. Vowels, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Exact propositional model counting admits dynamic programs parameterized by primal, dual, and incidence treewidth.
source_refs.author: Marko Samer, Stefan Szeider

source_refs.claim: Independent-edge source-to-target reliability is exactly computable by a fixed-parameter algorithm on bounded-treewidth networks.
source_refs.author: Amir Kafshdar Goharshady, Fatemeh Mohammadi

open_problems.why_unsolved: Network-reliability dynamic programs track connectivity states of the original network, whereas the causal failure predicate is represented by a hypergraph whose vertices are uncertain causal edges and whose hyperedges are minimal hedge supports. Generic incidence-treewidth model counting provides broad machinery, but a causal result still requires an exact reduction of successful ID realizations to obstruction-free sets, bag states for partially witnessed obstruction supports, bit-complexity control for exact rational arithmetic, and a simultaneous derivative computation rather than one complete rerun per edge.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An identity R_XY(p)=prod_e(1-p_e)I_O((p_e/(1-p_e))_e), extended polynomially to boundary probabilities, and an incidence-decomposition dynamic program returning R_XY and all partial derivatives in 2^{O(tau)} times a polynomial in input and output bit length.

writing_exemplar.why: Its probabilistic-ADMG framing makes total identification probability and edge-refinement sensitivity natural outputs beyond a single selected graph.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: edges have epistemic probabilities -> edgeID chooses a plausible identifiable realization -> one realization does not quantify total confidence -> compute exact identification mass and marginal edge sensitivities

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over bottom-up incidence-treewidth tables that record assignments and satisfied constraints, replacing clauses with obstruction hyperedges and integer counts with rational weights.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Avoiding every minimal failure support is a weighted monotone model-counting problem on precisely the support-edge incidence graph.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt project-join elimination over a sum-product semiring, augmenting each table value with derivative payloads propagated by the product rule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested reliability polynomial is a literal-weighted model count, and its full gradient can be transported through the same arithmetic circuit.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt reliability-preserving decomposition and boundary-state merging, with obstruction-satisfaction states replacing connectivity partitions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the closest exact independent-edge reliability algorithm parameterized by tree-likeness.

open_problems.open_problem: Is exact counting of edge realizations in which P_x(y) is identifiable #P-complete even for topologically ordered uncertain ADMG envelopes whose largest bidirected district has size two?

source_refs.claim: Finding an optimal identifiable realization in a probabilistic ADMG is NP-complete, but the complexity of counting all identifiable realizations is not classified.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Fateme Jamshidi, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Matthew J. Vowels, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Source-sink reliability remains #P-complete for acyclic directed planar graphs of maximum degree three.
source_refs.author: J. Scott Provan

source_refs.claim: Classical reliability and enumeration problems furnish foundational #P-completeness reductions for counting successful component configurations.
source_refs.author: Leslie G. Valiant

open_problems.why_unsolved: NP-completeness of selecting a best identifiable graph does not imply #P-hardness of summing all identifiable realizations. A causal counting reduction must map source-to-target witnesses to edge realizations without uncontrolled multiplicity, keep directed edges acyclic and topologically ordered, preserve the district-size-two restriction, and prove that the designated query fails ordinary ID exactly on the encoded reliability event. Classical reliability reductions do not supply hedge equivalence or the bidirected-width invariant.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A parsimonious or counting-preserving polynomial-time reduction from acyclic directed source-sink reliability to successful-realization counting at p_e=1/2 for b=2 uncertain ADMG envelopes, together with a proof of membership in #P.

writing_exemplar.why: It establishes the optimization-complexity baseline in precisely the uncertain-ADMG setting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: probabilistic causal graphs induce exponentially many realizations -> selecting the best identifiable realization is NP-complete -> total confidence requires summing all successful realizations -> classify that exact sum even under tiny districts

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the counting reduction for acyclic directed source-sink reliability, replacing operative paths with deterministic ancestry witnesses inside size-two hedge gadgets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The b<=2 causal obstruction is expected to collapse to directed reachability, while Provan's reduction already preserves acyclicity.

method_exemplars.technique: Use hedge completeness in both directions to prove that a reduced graph realization is nonidentifiable exactly when the encoded reliability event occurs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A counting-preserving reduction needs a necessary-and-sufficient causal obstruction, not merely a sufficient graphical pattern.

open_problems.open_problem: Can exact causal-identification reliability and factor sensitivities be extended from mutually independent uncertain edges to block-correlated or factor-graph edge uncertainty with complexity controlled by combined obstruction-factor incidence treewidth?

source_refs.claim: The main theory assumes mutually independent edges; its conclusion names failure of independence as future work, while its appendix handles only perfect positive or negative correlations.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Fateme Jamshidi, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Matthew J. Vowels, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Its extended reliability model permits arbitrary dependence within edge blocks while retaining independence across blocks.
source_refs.author: Amir Kafshdar Goharshady, Fatemeh Mohammadi

source_refs.claim: Project-join-tree dynamic programming computes exact weighted model counts and provides an architecture for incorporating local factors.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey M. Dudek, Vu H. N. Phan, Moshe Y. Vardi
source_refs.venue: International Conference on Principles and Practice of Constraint Programming

open_problems.why_unsolved: The product normalization into an ordinary multivariate independence polynomial is the first proof step that fails when edge indicators are dependent. Perfect equality or complement constraints cover only degenerate correlations, whereas learned structural uncertainty may couple many incident edges. A tractable result must combine local probability factors with obstruction constraints, define a width measure controlling both structures, prevent double counting across overlapping factors, and propagate derivatives with respect to factor parameters rather than independent marginal edge probabilities.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A factorized weighted-model-count characterization and junction-tree algorithm returning exact identification probability and every local-factor parameter derivative in 2^{O(k)} polynomial exact-arithmetic time, where k is the treewidth of the combined edge-factor-obstruction incidence graph.

writing_exemplar.why: The paper explicitly isolates independence as a limitation while motivating edge probabilities as beliefs or test confidence, for which dependence is scientifically natural.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: edge confidence is represented probabilistically -> independence enables additive edgeID objectives -> learned or elicited edge beliefs are often dependent -> compute identification reliability under structured dependence

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over arbitrary distributions on correlated edge blocks and reliability-preserving boundary contraction, replacing connectivity with hedge-support avoidance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates that local edge dependence can remain compatible with exact tree-decomposition reliability computation.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent correlation blocks as local weighted factors and use project-join elimination to sum factor products subject to obstruction-avoidance constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired quantity becomes a factorized weighted model count once edge independence is replaced by a graphical probability model.

open_problems.open_problem: Can identifiable uncertain-ADMG realizations be partitioned canonically into semantically distinct identifying-functional classes, with duplicate-free enumeration and exact probability mass for every class?

source_refs.claim: The paper optimizes graphs and the aggregate validity of a selected formula but does not partition all realizations by semantic equality of their identifying functionals.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Fateme Jamshidi, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Matthew J. Vowels, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: For MPDAG uncertainty, the paper recursively enumerates subclasses yielding distinct total-effect functionals and removes duplicate outputs.
source_refs.author: F. Richard Guo, Emilija Perkovic

source_refs.claim: The paper automatically simplifies graph-derived causal expressions but does not give a complete semantic equivalence test across ADMG realizations.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Juha Karvanen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Different realizations can yield syntactically different ID traces whose functionals are algebraically equal, while identical-looking syntax can rely on different graph-specific validity conditions. Maximizing one representative graph therefore need not find the functional class with greatest total probability. The MPDAG solution exploits adjustment and orientation structure, but latent-confounded ADMGs introduce nested district factorization and front-door-like expressions; graph-aware expression simplification alone is not a sound-and-complete semantic classifier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound-and-complete canonical-normal-form or graph-theoretic equivalence characterization for ordinary-ID functionals, plus a duplicate-free algorithm enumerating every equivalence class and its exact summed realization probability.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formula-validity objective directly motivates replacing graph-level plausibility with functional-class probability mass.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: one uncertain envelope supports many graphs -> identifiable graphs can imply different formulas -> graph probability is not functional-class probability -> aggregate and report every semantically distinct identifying functional

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt recursive subclass splitting with a uniqueness invariant so that each output denotes one distinct causal functional rather than one graph.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the duplicate-functional problem for Markov-equivalence uncertainty, though without latent-confounded district structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Use graph-aware elimination of unnecessary variables and factors as a normalization layer before equivalence classification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Canonical simplification is the first required step for merging ID outputs that differ only through redundant summations or factors.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit recursive district decomposition to attach canonical graphical provenance to each identified functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The classes must cover the full family of functionals produced by complete ADMG identification.

open_problems.open_problem: For a discrete observational law and a probabilistic ADMG envelope, can one compute the probability distribution of realization-specific sharp causal-bound intervals, including the probability that interval width is at most epsilon and its sensitivity to every uncertain edge?

source_refs.claim: The conclusion explicitly proposes extending its uncertain-graph point-identification methodology to partial identification.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Fateme Jamshidi, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Matthew J. Vowels, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Discrete causal queries reduce to polynomial programs whose global optima give sharp bounds, with certified outer ranges during computation.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper derives analytical causal-effect bounds from a PAG representing a Markov-equivalence class, combining structural uncertainty and partial identification without enumerating every graph.
source_refs.author: Alexis Bellot

open_problems.why_unsolved: Boolean hedge supports exploit monotonicity of point nonidentifiability, but sharp bound endpoints depend on the observational law and graph-specific latent response-function constraints. Adding an edge enlarges the model class without generally producing a simple threshold event for interval width, so the obstruction hypergraph alone cannot aggregate partial-identification quality. Autobounds treats one fixed causal model, while PAG bounds concern an unweighted equivalence class rather than a probability distribution over independently selected directed and bidirected edges.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graph-native characterization and exact or certified algorithm for the weighted distribution of sharp intervals [L_G(P),U_G(P)] over realizations, with theorems for Pr(U_G-L_G<=epsilon), edgewise derivatives, and sharpness or epsilon-sharpness.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly names partial identification as a destination for uncertain causal networks and supplies the practical graph-probability setting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: uncertain edges make point identification probabilistic -> likely nonidentified realizations can still imply informative bounds -> bound quality varies across realizations -> quantify the probability of achieving a desired sharp-bound width

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over response-function polynomial parameterization, dual relaxation, and spatial branch-and-bound to compute certified endpoints for each compressed structural state.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested random interval is assembled from the same sharp discrete causal bounds, evaluated across graph realizations.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt invariant-property arguments that bound effects across a structural equivalence class, replacing an unweighted PAG class with a weighted edge-realization family.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly combines graphical structural ambiguity with causal bounds and may permit compression beyond realization-by-realization optimization.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt calibrated projection and bootstrap relaxation of estimated inequality constraints to obtain uniformly valid confidence regions for aggregated bound endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After graph-weighted endpoints are characterized, sampling uncertainty makes them projections of a partially identified parameter vector.

literature_map:
Akbari et al. (2023, NeurIPS, arXiv:2208.04627) introduce probabilistic ADMGs and edgeID, optimizing a plausible identifiable graph rather than total identification probability.
Their main theory assumes mutually independent edge indicators; Appendix C covers perfect correlations, while the conclusion identifies general dependence as future work.
The same conclusion proposes carrying the uncertain-network methodology from point identification to partial identification.
Shpitser and Pearl (2008, JMLR, DOI:10.5555/1390681.1442797) establish complete ADMG identification and graphical nonidentifiability certificates for fixed graphs.
Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2022, ICML, arXiv:2205.02232) connect intervention design to hitting minimal hedges and use lazy hedge discovery for optimization.
Guo and Perkovic (2021, AISTATS, arXiv:2010.08611) give duplicate-free enumeration of distinct total-effect functionals over MPDAG subclasses, but not probabilistic latent-confounded ADMGs.
Tikka and Karvanen (2017, JMLR, arXiv:1806.07082) simplify graphical identifying expressions without supplying complete semantic equivalence across graph realizations.
Khachiyan et al. (2007, Discrete Applied Mathematics, DOI:10.1016/j.dam.2006.04.032) study output-sensitive path/cut conjunction enumeration and give a directed special case with polynomial delay.
Mary (2026 revision, arXiv:2407.00694) obtains incremental-polynomial minimal-transversal enumeration under bounded VC dimension; unrestricted hypergraph dualization remains open.
Samer and Szeider (2010, Journal of Discrete Algorithms, DOI:10.1016/j.jda.2009.06.002) give exact model-counting algorithms parameterized by incidence treewidth.
Dudek, Phan, and Vardi (2020, CP, arXiv:2008.08748) formulate weighted model counting through project-join dynamic programming.
Goharshady and Mohammadi (2020, Reliability Engineering & System Safety, arXiv:1712.09692) give exact bounded-treewidth network reliability and permit arbitrary dependence inside local edge blocks.
Valiant (1979, DOI:10.1137/0208032) and Provan (1986, DOI:10.1137/0215050) establish #P-completeness for classical reliability, including acyclic directed source-sink reliability.
Duarte et al. (2024, JASA, arXiv:2109.13471) compute certified sharp bounds for discrete causal models; Bellot (2023, arXiv:2311.07259) derives bounds under PAG uncertainty.
The unoccupied intersection is hedge-complete minimal uncertain-edge support enumeration, exact probability and gradient aggregation, and tight counting complexity under bounded ADMG district size.
